name: 05-duplication-divergence
title: Duplication–divergence (biological growth)
question: Does genome-style duplication-and-divergence reproduce protein-network topology?
hypothesis: Copying a random node's neighbourhood and pruning edges yields a heavy-tailed, locally clustered network like observed protein-interaction graphs.
objective: Run the duplication_divergence reaction and show how it reconfigures the network, measuring its signature structural observables.
description:
Copy-then-diverge growth reproduces the heavy-tailed, locally clustered topology seen in protein-interaction networks.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `duplication_divergence` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
claim: Copy-then-diverge growth reproduces the heavy-tailed, locally clustered topology seen in protein-interaction networks.

findings.summary: Copy-then-diverge growth reproduces the heavy-tailed, locally clustered topology seen in protein-interaction networks.
findings.detail: Duplication reinforces hubs while the shared-neighbour mechanism raises clustering above a random graph — the combination that distinguishes biological growth from BA.
